body:
Indianapolis may be rebuilding, but Taylor's team-friendly contract and place among the NFL's most productive running backs gave the franchise little reason to accept a discounted offer

        Jonathan Taylor isn't going anywhere. The Indianapolis Colts decided to keep their 27-year-old, three-time Pro Bowl running back at the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The Colts  turned down offers of second-round picks and more for Taylor, indicating they required at least a first-round pick to trade him away, according to Tom Pelissero.Basically, it seems like Indianapolis turned down trade offers comparable to what the San Francisco 49ers sent the Carolina Panthers in 2022 to acquire running back Christian McCaffrey, who was 26. Back then, San Francisco sent Carolina the following picks: a 2023 second-round pick, a 2023 third-round pick, a 2023 fourth-round pick and a 2024 fifth-round pick. So why would the Colts walk away from such a deal for Taylor? Let's break it down. 
The Colts are overcompensating in their Taylor trade demands after not getting market value for Quenton Nelson (a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick from the Seattle Seahawks). They also don't have their own first-round pick ahead of the highly anticipated 2027 NFL Draft because they traded it to the New York Jets a year ago to acquire cornerback Sauce Gardner. That's why Indianapolis probably rebuffed trade packages that lacked first-round picks: they were trying to clean up their mistake from last year's trade deadline. Also, Taylor is one of the best running backs of his generation: he averages the fifth-most rushing yards per game (88.8) in NFL history. It's understandable why Indianapolis maintained the stance that they won't trade him away for anything less than a first-round pick.
Most rushing yards per game, NFL historyRush YPGJim Brown104.3Barry Sanders99.8Terrell Davis97.5Eric Dickerson90.8Jonathan Taylor88.8Walter Payton88.0The running back contract market has also changed, and they were able to lock Taylor down on a two-year, $44 million extension with $39 million in guaranteed money before the 2026 season began. That's a great value. The Colts now have him locked down through the 2028 season, the rest of his 20s, and there isn't any guaranteed money left on the deal in 2027 or 2028. That makes it really easy to move him via trade in the future or keep him around for whatever quarterback they eventually add to replace Daniel Jones next year. Those are the reasons why Taylor won't be relocating at the 2026 NFL trade deadline on Tuesday afternoon.

title: Kirk Cousins trade grades: Vikings hope to salvage offense; Raiders get 'A,' turn to Fernando Mendoza - CBS Sports
description: Cousins returns to the place he played from 2018-23
body:
Cousins returns to the place he played from 2018-23

                    at
    3:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings are making one last-ditch attempt to save their offense, reuniting with Kirk Cousins and sending their 2027 third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders in return.Cousins, 38, was in the middle of a renaissance year in Sin City, with 20 passing touchdowns and just eight interceptions. He is now being called upon to save a dire situation in Minneapolis. The Vikings have scored just 11 offensive touchdowns this season, tied with the Chargers for the fewest in the NFL. Offseason addition Kyler Murray and veteran backup Carson Wentz have both struggled mightily, with Murray at or near the bottom of most major passing categories and Wentz throwing for just 81 yards and two interceptions starting for Murray (hamstring) on "Monday Night Football."Cousins spent 2018-23 in Minnesota, where he made three of his four career Pro Bowls. He was especially good in 2022, when he led an NFL-high eight game-winning drives, and Minnesota went 13-4 before being bounced in its first playoff game. The next year, Cousins was arguably even better — on pace for maybe the best year of his career — before tearing his Achilles. Now, three years later, he gets to leave a different lasting legacy in Minnesota.Teammates until Monday, Fernando Mendoza and Cousins now step into very different spotlights. The Raiders will hope the Mendoza era lasts for years to come and that he can make some positive strides this year. The Vikings, on the other hand, are all-in on this year. Here's how both teams fared:

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota Vikings: B-That the Vikings are even in this situation is worthy of an "F." Ever since Cousins left, they have failed to find a suitable replacement: Sam Darnold was excellent in 2024, but the Vikings let him go in favor of J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy played poorly and was hurt several times last year, as the Vikings rode a quarterback carousel. Minnesota traded McCarthy, who had been demoted to third-string behind Murray and Wentz, to the Giants early this season. Murray — always a curious-at-best fit for this offense — clearly wasn't cutting it, and Wentz was never going to, either.Cousins has been good this year — not great, but good. He looks far better than what he had been in Atlanta, where it was clear his mobility hadn't returned post-Achilles tear. He's still never going to win with his athleticism, but his negative play rate is down to 6.7%, on pace for a career best, and he is only being sacked on 9.8% of his dropbacks, also on pace for a career best. How much of that praise belongs to Klint Kubiak is up for debate, but it's clear Cousins has regained some of his spryness. He doesn't have to be Michael Vick, but he can't be a statue.Really, though, this all comes down to fit. Murray never fit. Cousins, hypothetically, does. Obviously, there is proof of concept here given his past in Minnesota. He attacks the middle of the field and delivers on intermediate throws. Plus, he is comfortable off play action. These are crucial parts of O'Connell's scheme. Cousins, if nothing else, should do a much, much better job keeping the offense on schedule.
Passing success rate this yearKirk CousinsKyler MurrayOverall50%39%Between   numbers57%52%Throws   10-20 yards downfield57%44%Play   action60%48%Given the circumstances, this grade can only be so high, and given the solution, it cannot get that much higher. Cousins is not a star. His arm strength is not what it once was, and for all the good things he did in Las Vegas, he is coming off a three-interception game. We'll see how he holds up, physically, over the rigors of an 18-game regular season (he will not get a bye) plus expected postseason. His accuracy is a bit down from his best years, though it's still a clear major improvement over Murray and Wentz, who at times seemed unable to hit water if they fell off a boat.It's also nice that the Vikings still have a third-round pick — the Eagles' from the Jonathan Greenard trade — next year. It will be better than Minnesota's, too.Even though Cousins can unlock the best part of this offense — Justin Jefferson, who is the biggest winner of this deal — he cannot fix everything. The offensive line has been up-and-down at best, and the running game has been poor. Minnesota's running backs are 31st in percentage of carries with a missed tackle forced and 26th in EPA per rush. There's not much juice there.
Overall, Minnesota got better with this trade. Much better. But it couldn't get much worse, either. Even with a truly outstanding defense, is average-to-slightly-above-average quarterback play and, in turn, average offense good enough to cash in on Super Bowl aspirations? The Vikings are about to find out, but at least they're giving themselves a chance.P.S. O'Connell had better be right about this move. He has missed on two straight quarterback evaluations. He cannot miss on a third.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Raiders: AIf you told a Raiders fan before the season that Mendoza would make his first start in Week 10, they'd probably say that's about right. If you told them he'd start because the Raiders got a top-100 pick for Cousins, they'd be very happy with that outcome.
Cousins well exceeded the mere placeholder role he was given. He played well and, at times, very well. He kept an offense that's very much in the early building stage moving — the Raiders are eighth in points per drive this season. He did this all alongside one of the league's worst running games and worst/youngest wide receiver corps. He leaned on Brock Bowers, who looks like a superstar once again, and fellow tight end Michael Mayer. The Raiders went 4-5 under Cousins and were competitive in several losses. This was a 99th-percentile outcome.Now, it's Mendoza's turn. It's a little bit tough to drop him into the starting role in these circumstances — not knowing he's starting until Tuesday, and facing Seattle's ferocious defense — but that will be of little matter in the long haul. Kubiak did a great job with Cousins, and the fruits of his labor are a valuable draft pick as Las Vegas continues its build. Strong work all around.

With that in mind, here are Tuesday's hot stove rumors.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Mets will meet with Skubal 
The Mets have a meeting scheduled with two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, the clear top free agent avaiable this offseason, later this week, reports the New York Post. Skubal will meet with teams in California, presumably at the offices of agent Scott Boras. Owner Steve Cohen is expected to push for Skubal, according to SNY; president of baseball operations David Stearns has long been reluctant to sign big-money, long-term deals for pitchers, though pitchers of Skubal's caliber are rarely available. The Mets are also seeking first base help and bullpen reinforcements.Nolan McLean and Christian Scott are the only locks for New York's 2027 rotation at the moment. Justin Hagenman, Sean Manaea, Kodai Senga, Zac Thornton, and Jonah Tong are next in line to make starts. Tylor Megill is expected back from Tommy John surgery early next year as well. The Mets have some depth but clearly need more impact. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Blue Jays interested in Lowe 
The Blue Jays are among the teams with interest in free agent second baseman Brandon Lowe, according to Sportsnet. Ernie Clement, Toronto's primary second baseman in 2026, crashed hard in the second half and has always fit better as a super utility man who plays regularly at different positions. Josh Smith is the team's other second base option. Lowe would bring needed power to a team that finished dead last in home runs this past season and had just one player, Kazuma Okamoto (33), clear 15 home runs. Only four Blue Jays hit even 10 homers. Also, Toronto's lineup is mostly right-handed. Lowe would add power and also a lefty bat to provide balance. We ranked him as the 13th-best free agent available. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Rotation help a 'top priority' for White Sox Adding rotation help is a "top priority," White Sox GM Chris Getz said during an MLB Network Radio interview on Tuesday. "We're going to exhaust the starter market, both free agency -- we'll take a look -- along with trades. That is our top priority," Getz said. He also confirmed that Grant Taylor, the team's postseason closer, will move into the rotation. Hagen Smith will remain in the bullpen. 
The White Sox have solid enough rotation depth with Taylor joining Sean Burke, Luis Castillo, Anthony Kay, Davis Martin, David Sandlin, Noah Schultz, and perhaps Shane Smith and Drew Thorpe. There is room for improvement, though, particularly at the top. Chicago could use a bona fide ace, not that one is easy to acquire or abundantly available. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Padres have expressed interest in Skubal   Add the Padres to the list of teams that have shown interest in Skubal, reports MLB Network. San Diego has a major need in the rotation -- Joe Musgrove, who hasn't made a start since the 2024 postseason, and Randy Vásquez are their only rotation locks -- and a new ownership group that seems willing to spend in its first offseason.   Skubal is far and away the offseason's best free agent. He is also a Scott Boras client, and, historically, top Boras clients take the largest contract offer regardless of team situation. That isn't to say the Padres are a bad situation. Not at all. They're a very good team that is in the postseason most years, plus they play in San Diego. Who doesn't love San Diego?   
The Padres are also connected to several Japanese players, according to The Athletic. That includes MLB free agents Seiya Suzuki and Shota Imanaga, as well as players coming over from Nippon Professional Baseball, like third baseman Teruaki Sato. 
        
            
                MLB free agency: Six international players to know for the 2026-27 offseason
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
   Morejon prefers to stay in the bullpen   
Free agent lefty Adrian Morejon is drawing interest as a starting pitcher, but he prefers to remain in the bullpen, according to The Athletic. Even during the season, there were rumblings that Morejon would like to be given a chance to start in 2027. He came up through the minors as a starter and only remained in the bullpen because he was so dominant in a late-inning role.   We ranked Morejon as the offseason's second-best free agent on the idea that he would move into the rotation. The belief within the game is that he has a chance to be an excellent starter, not just a back-end piece. Either way, Morejon is a very good pitcher, and at 28, he's also one of the youngest free agents available. He should have several peak years remaining.   

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Cubs hope to add three starters Although they are disinclined to pursue Tarik Skubal, the Cubs hope to add three established starting pitchers this offseason, reports The Athletic. Of the nine pitchers to make at least nine starts for Chicago in 2027, seven are free agents. Only Ben Brown, who recently had neck surgery (per ESPN), and Edward Cabrera, who had a 5.96 ERA and was demoted to the bullpen, remain. Left-hander Justin Steele is expected back from UCL surgery next year, though he suffered a setback this summer and wasn't able to return as hoped in September. Others like Javier Assad and Jordan Wicks are depth options more than full-time rotation pieces. This free agent class offers plenty of second- and third-tier starters. That's where the Cubs are expected to shop. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Mets not interested in major overhaul   Unlike last offseason, the Mets are not interested in a major overhaul despite their disappointing year, reports MLB.com. The Mets went 74-88 and finished in last place in 2026. The only silver lining to the disappointing season was the ability to give a long runway to rookies like Carson Benge and Nolan McLean, both of whom finished in the top four of the Rookie of the Year voting.   
The Mets went 83-79 in 2025 and missed the postseason on the final day of the season. They made significant changes last winter, most notably jettisoning stalwarts Pete Alonso and Brandon Nimmo, then had a worse season in 2026. In September, president of baseball operations David Stearns admitted that much turnover created an "uncapped downside scenario," which is executive-speak for "there was too much risk." 
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Braves will not move Acuña   
Not surprisingly, the Braves are uninterested in moving former National League MVP Ronald Acuña Jr., according to MLB Network. It does feel like Atlanta's offense has gone stale and that they could move a core piece, but it won't be Acuña, nor is it likely to be Drake Baldwin, Michael Harris II, or Matt Olson. Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley are the more obvious players to move. Albies is entering the final season of his wildly team-friendly contract. Riley has six years remaining on his deal, which figures to make a move difficult.   
                            
    
                                                
                    
       Red Sox won't commit to Story at short   
On Monday, Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow declined to commit to Trevor Story as his starting shortstop next season. "We still have a ton of confidence in Trevor, but any decisions like that are going to take place between Trevor and me far before I speak to anything publicly," Breslow told reporters, including the Boston Globe. Boston has one of the top prospects in the minors in shortstop Franklin Arias, who is very likely to make his debut early next year. Arias could push Story into a utility role or off the team entirely.

title: Mauricio Pochettino's links to United a natural consequence of USMNT's big swing - CBS Sports
description: Pochettino is reportedly a contender for the United job, which is expected to free up shortly with the departure
body:
Pochettino is reportedly a contender for the United job, which is expected to free up shortly with the departure of Michael Carrick
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:44 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The patterns of the international match calendar are well known at this point. Players pack their suitcases, board planes, spend a small stretch of days with their compatriots … and in the U.S. men's national team's case, answer questions about their coach landing a new job.From the moment Mauricio Pochettino walked into a midtown Manhattan auditorium two years ago to make his opening remarks as the USMNT head coach, his presence has felt temporary to many. It was not just because job security is an increasingly unrealistic concept for soccer coaches, nor was it only down to the fact that Pochettino initially signed a deal that would expire 22 months later. The last two years have been full of reminders that the USMNT job is one of several that could be available to him – he has openly talked about wanting to return to the Premier League, did not deny that his representatives may have met with AC Milan in the weeks before the World Cup and regularly talks about his undying love for Tottenham Hotspur. The latest iteration of a years-long pattern came Tuesday, when reports out of England suggested Pochettino was a top contender for the Manchester United gig, which is not vacant yet but will be once the club finally parts ways with Michael Carrick.The cadence is unusual, since coaches rarely invite reasonable questions about seeking employment elsewhere. At this stage of Pochettino's tenure with the U.S. team, though, it would be difficult to characterize it as a surprise. It would be equally hard to argue that the pattern does not come with the territory, defender Antonee Robinson acknowledging as much hours after the news broke."That news kind of got sprung on us, like the rest of the world, I'd say," he said. "Similar things happened in the past, happened at the World Cup where huge teams lose their manager and they start looking at possible candidates and for us to have a manager who's linked with those sorts of jobs means we're very lucky to work with a top-level manager but it never seems to leak into the work we do, whether it's the World Cup or whether it's going to be this camp."
Pochettino's wantaway pattern may be annoying but it reflects the overarching sentiment of his tenure with the USMNT thus far. He is easily the highest-profile coach to take the job and U.S. Soccer is well aware of that. It is why they lined up donors to secure his signature two years ago to make him the federation's highest-paid coach ever, and why there is reportedly a $10 million buyout clause in the new deal he signed after the World Cup. For the first time in the program's modern history, they hired a coach with genuine international appeal. Even if Robinson should instead spend his time talking about the upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, the fact that Pochettino would be courted by others was baked into his appeal."Even when we first met a couple summers ago, there were lots of other people interested in having Mauricio and team join," U.S. Soccer CEO J.T. Batson said in May as chatter around the Milan job took center stage in the early days of the USMNT's World Cup preparations. "He had standing offers from other places to come. He wanted to be here. He's a big believer in what we're doing at U.S. Soccer. He's a big believer in soccer in America and he's a big believer in this men's team and so, throughout this entire process, when you have top-class talent, whether it's salespeople, whether it's marketing people or whether it's coaches, other organizations want them and throughout this, Mauricio and team have been incredibly transparent. They've been great partners and are, of course, excited about the summer … There's been a longer list of outreach than what has even been reported and so they've been great about that."The key difference here is that he reportedly might be interested in United's offer, according to the Guardian, but the situation remains the same, despite the timing being strange, three months after agreeing a four-year deal. If Pochettino does not end up on United's touchline, his time with the USMNT was never destined to last forever, and U.S. Soccer admitted to it months ago.
"We actually, on a monthly basis, have a succession planning session for all of our coaches across all of our teams and so as a part of that, we have plans for renewals," Batson said on that May day. "We have plans for interims and we have plans for replacements because you never know what's going to happen. It's a global sport, lots going on and so that's a standard part of us growing up as U.S. Soccer."Where should the USMNT go from here?Many might spend the subsequent weeks after Pochettino's hypothetical departure questioning Batson's claim that the Argentine is actually a "big believer in soccer in America," though the argument is irrelevant as far as the USMNT goes. Pochettino's hire, along with that of U.S. women's national team head coach Emma Hayes a year earlier, was a large statement of intent from U.S. Soccer's leaders like Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, who are relatively new to their jobs. Pochettino's exit, therefore, would raise the question of how they continue that vision two years later, especially after outlining an ambitious path for the men's program in the coming years.High-profile candidates like Pochettino are not exactly easy to come by, as the initial effort to hire him demonstrated. Ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola is easily the most notable name on the market but it is entirely unclear what his next coaching move might be, even if that should not discourage U.S. Soccer from reaching out if they have a vacancy. The options thin out from there if they are only to be measured on their flair, though, making it hard to envision a perfect follow-up act to Pochettino in the short term.
There is a theory that U.S. Soccer may be resigned to picking from a locally sourced talent pool, something that is reinforced by a suggestion that Pochettino was a false steward of American soccer. His departure, if it comes in the short term, is not actually an indictment on U.S. Soccer's approach, nor should it encourage the federation to go for the safest pick next. Pochettino's tenure, at least up until this point, has been an example in reaping rewards for a bold strategy, one that should continue long after he is gone.Pochettino's time with the USMNT has so far been characterized by mixed results, including some low lows that he bears just as much responsibility for as his players. It is not hard to see why he was a good fit for the job, though, and it is not because he makes headlines – his high-intensity, attack-minded style of play actually suited the player pool. The fact that he has coached in a UEFA Champions League final and won a Ligue 1 title with Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar may help with player buy-in, but it would not have papered over the cracks if his version of the USMNT was not actually a decent marriage between his tactical preferences and the players' natural skillsets.He continues to feel like a good fit in the post-World Cup months, especially as he oversees a generational shift in the player pool. Pochettino's tenure at Spurs, where he initially made a name for himself as a coach, was defined by his trust in young players but as it pertains to the USMNT's up-and-comers specifically, they already seem well-positioned to slot into his tactical set-up. The team's next great prospects are almost all exclusively attackers; Neil Pierre, the Philadelphia Union 19-year-old in the midst of a breakout season, is so far one of the few notable exceptions at center back.
A quote-unquote big name might not be a realistic option for the USMNT if Pochettino leaves now, though he may have theoretically made the gig more attractive to prospective coaches. More importantly, though, U.S. Soccer is now well-positioned to make a hire based on style and specifically an entertaining and effective style that captured the attention of an otherwise uninterested nation during the World Cup. Straying from that, no matter if Pochettino's successor is world renowned or otherwise, would not match the potential of the USMNT's rising stars, nor would it align with U.S. Soccer's own vision.

title: Greg Schiano is staying, but Rutgers' bigger problem is the cost of keeping up in the Big Ten - CBS Sports

body:
Saddled with mounting debt, poor on-field results and diminishing television value, the Scarlet Knights are turning into an expensive liability for their conference
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Rutgers wants to be in the Big Ten, it just doesn't want to act like a Big Ten school.Rutgers announced Tuesday that longtime head coach Greg Schiano will be back for the 2027 season. There had been plenty of speculation building about Schiano's status at the school as Rutgers is off to a 2-7 start, ensuring it will miss out on a bowl game for the second consecutive season. The Knights are also only 3-12 in Big Ten play over the last two seasons.Even when you consider what Greg Schiano has meant to the program -- his 101 wins are 23 more than any other coach in program history, and he's been the coach for nine of the school's 13 bowl games -- those are the kind of results that tend to lead to changes.Yet, in the announcement that Schiano would be returning, Rutgers athletics director Keli Zinn made it clear that this decision had nothing to do with accepting the results.
"Our results are not acceptable for the expectations we have for our football program and for the athletics program we are building," Zinn said. "However, I also have an obligation to make decisions that serve the best long-term interests of Rutgers University."Let me be very clear: this decision is not reflective of a lowering of standards or an indication that everything is fine. It is not. This is instead a reflection of my belief that we have an opportunity to make meaningful changes that will strengthen our roster and better position our program to compete and win at a higher level."I'll translate that for you: "We know we're not playing well enough right now but we don't have the money to pay Greg Schiano and his staff to go away, replace them with a new one, and then be able to put a roster on the field that can compete."If Rutgers were to fire Schiano now, it would owe him a little more than a $17 million buyout. A hefty price for sure, but in the grand scheme of college football, it is not an exorbitant amount, which gets to the heart of the issue with Rutgers, at least from the Big Ten's perspective.Rutgers enjoys being a Big Ten school, it just can't afford to live in the neighborhood anymore.I understand why Rutgers is making the decision. The athletic department dealt with a $78 million deficit for the 2024-25 season. It truly does not have the money to make this move, and asking them to spend more money to overhaul everything would be fiscally irresponsible.The school was already in trouble financially when former Big Ten commissioner Jim Delany went for The Great Cable Box Heist of 2012. Rutgers was an athletic department in need of cash, and the Big Ten was a conference in need of cable boxes for its network. So Rutgers agreed to join at a serious discount for the infusion of short-term gains, while the Big Ten got their network on cable in the New York/New Jersey metro area.
The problem is the cost of running an athletic department has skyrocketed since. You aren't just paying coaches anymore, you're paying players, and they're essentially free agents. The price of playing poker in a league like the Big Ten isn't getting cheaper any time soon, and Rutgers has struggled to keep up.From a competitive standpoint, Rutgers isn't bringing much of anything to the league. As we enter an era of the 24-team playoff in which 19 spots in the field will go to at-large bids, Rutgers could prove to be a drag on the resumes of all the Big Ten schools actually competing for those spots. There's a reason 3-loss SEC teams get treated as playoff contenders and 3-loss Big Ten teams don't, and it's not just because SEC coaches are better at lobbying.I mean, when Rutgers is losing non-conference games to UMass, any Big Ten team that beats it doesn't have much of an argument to make about the value of that win. The problem isn't related strictly to football, either. Rutgers joined the Big Ten in 2014. It's only reached the NCAA Tournament twice in men's basketball, which is th
Further complicating matters is the fact that those cable boxes Rutgers brought to the Big Ten over a decade ago don't matter much, if at all, anymore. When the league's current television deal expires, and it shops it around to networks, I don't know that any of them will be clamoring for Rutgers games to be made available to them. While the current iteration of the Protect College Sports Act (PCSA) seems less likely to pass following recent mid-term election results, part of the act was to cap the number of teams a conference can have in it. If whatever the new form of the bill is in the future has the same provision, how long until conferences do what was once unthinkable and kick schools out to bring new ones in? Rutgers bringing back Schiano for at least one more season seems to be the financially prudent thing for the athletic department, and Rutgers' first priority should always be to do what's best for Rutgers. But is Rutgers what's best for the Big Ten? That's a question likely to come up at Big Ten headquarters, if it hasn't already, and Rutgers would be wise to close out the 2020s with a better sense of the moment.

title: Chiefs agree to acquire WR Josh Downs in trade with Colts, per report - CBS Sports
description: Indianapolis' rebuild is a benefit to Kansas City, which secured much-needed help in its receiving corps
body:
Indianapolis' rebuild is a benefit to Kansas City, which secured much-needed help in its receiving corps
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        An influx of reciever talent is headed to the Kansas City Chiefs offense, as the team agreed to terms with the Indianapolis Colts on a trade for wide receiver Josh Downs. According to ESPN, the Chiefs will receive Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick and send a 2027 fourth-rounder and fifth-rounder back to Indianapolis.The Chiefs land an immediate-impact upgrade for their passing offense, which lacks depth and has become more one-dimensional than at any point in the Patrick Mahomes era. Mahomes now has another weapon to throw to alongside Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy and his stable of tight ends which includes Travis Kelce.Kansas City owns the 10th-best passing offense in the NFL but is more reliant on yards after the catch than any team in football. The downfield attack is not nearly as prolific as it was during the height of the Chiefs' offensive dominance. Downs was not much of a field-stretcher during his time with the Colts, seeing just 21 targets of 20-plus yards over the last three seasons in Indianapolis per NFL Next Gen Stats, but perhaps his arrival will either come with an expansion of his role or allow the existing receivers to run deeper routes.Chiefs wide receivers accounted for just 46.0% of the team's receiving yards through Week 9, which marked the second-lowest rate of any team, ahead of only the Las Vegas Raiders at 36.8%, according to Next Gen Stats.The concerning state of Kansas City's passing game also led to a reliance on running back Kenneth Walker III as both a ballcarrier and a receiver. He is the league's second-leading rusher and last week against the New York Jets recorded his first career games with multiple receiving touchdowns. Any addition to the receiving unit should help reduce some of the strain on the Chiefs' prized running back while also potentially opening up greater opportunities for him in the run game as defenses respect the pass to a greater extent.
Downs is the second Colts receiver to be moved in the hours leading up to the NFL trade deadline and follows Keenan Allen (who is headed to the San Francisco 49ers) as another casualty of the franchise's commitment to a rebuild. The Colts emerged as the biggest sellers of the deadline following a two-win start to the season.Indianapolis parted with four players who are on expiring contracts and thus secured draft capital for standouts who were likely to leave in free agency anyway. Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Allen and Downs netted the Colts a plethora of picks for them to use as they reconstruct their roster from the ground up under a new general manager who has yet to be hired.The fire sale leaves the Colts' wide receiver group barren. There are only five healthy receivers on the roster, including Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, who the team signed from its practice squad in the midst of its deadline day trade flurry. Those active receivers are as follows:Laquon TreadwellDeion BurksAshton DulinAnthony GouldNick Westbrook-IkhineStandout field-stretcher Alec Pierce is expected to return from injured reserve at some point this season, but the Colts have no reason to rush him back into action as they barrel toward a lost campaign.
You can follow the latest in trade deadline news via the CBS Sports live blog.

title: Keenan Allen trade grades: 49ers acquire WR help from Colts for Day 3 pick, per report - CBS Sports
description: San Francisco adds a veteran receiver at the trade deadline
body:
San Francisco adds a veteran receiver at the trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The San Francisco 49ers are adding another weapon for Brock Purdy as they gear up to race for the No. 1 seed in the NFC. At the trade deadline, the 49ers acquired veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts for a sixth-round pick, per ESPN. This is the second trade John Lynch and Colts interim general manager Ed Dodds have pulled off in the past few weeks, as the 49ers sent a fourth-round pick to Indianapolis for defensive lineman DeForest Buckner at the end of October. Allen, who turned 34 in April, signed a one-year deal with the Colts in August and has caught 40 passes for 351 yards and one touchdown in eight games played. During Sunday's loss to the Dallas Cowboys, he caught four passes for 26 yards. Allen's 40 receptions led the Colts prior to the trade and would lead all 49ers on the season. The 49ers were in the maket for wide receiver help, as Mike Evans (Achilles/ribs) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) have been sidelined in recent weeks. Christian Kirk was also recently placed on injured reserve with a knee injury, where he joins fellow injured wideouts Ricky Pearsall and De'Zhaun Stribling.  
Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Demarcus Robinson, KhaDarel Hodge and Jacob Cowing were Purdy's wide receivers during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. Watkins led the team with 86 yards on four receptions. The injuries haven't held San Francisco's offense back yet, as through Week 9, the 49ers rank sixth in yards per game (376.8) and third in points per game (29.4). This is a well-rounded team that registered two passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a defensive touchdown on Sunday for the first time since 2022.Allen is a six-time Pro Bowler that spent 12 of his 14 NFL seasons with the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers, and is the franchise's second-leading receiver behind Hall of Famer Antonio Gates. He has recorded six 1,000-yard seasons and five 100-catch seasons, which is tied for third all-time. Let's attempt to grade this trade: 49ers: BAccording to the Associated Press, the 49ers have had a record seven players 30 years or older catch touchdowns this season. Only the 1998 Denver Broncos, 2007 New England Patriots and 2002 Raiders have had more total touchdowns by different players 30 or older. Imagine going back in time and telling a 49ers fan that they would have Mike Evans and Keenan Allen at wide receiver. It's true that both are older players now, but Kyle Shanahan is going to be able to get the most out of them in his system. 
Allen still has some tread left on the tires, and he was the Colts' most reliable receiver despite the fact that he was not brought in to play that role. Alec Pierce has been sidelined by an ankle injury, while Josh Downs hasn't reached 25 yards receiving ever since his trade request went public. Just last year, Allen caught 81 passes for 777 yards and four touchdowns with the Chargers. The 49ers winning this trade of course hinges on health. It remains to be seen if Evans will be able to return to 100% this season with his Achilles strain, and if Allen can remain available as well. Ultimately, the 49ers didn't have to pay a high price for a veteran pass-catcher that could upgrade the offense. It's worth mentioning that Allen is facing a minimum three-game suspension following his OWI arrest in Indianapolis earlier this year, but we don't know when that suspension will be coming down. 
Colts: C+The Colts are obvious sellers at the trade deadline. They are losers of five straight, fired general manager Chris Ballard last month and have already shipped off Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner and now Keenan Allen. Allen wasn't helping the Colts win games by himself, and he was a piece Indy felt fine parting ways with prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. deadline. The more interesting storylines to follow with the Colts come after: what will Indianapolis end up doing with star running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs?

title: College Football Playoff Rankings prediction: Georgia takes top spot, rival SEC team joins top four - CBS Sports
description: The Bulldogs are set to top Tuesday's top 25 release, while multiple SEC teams on the wrong end of lopsided Week
body:
The Bulldogs are set to top Tuesday's top 25 release, while multiple SEC teams on the wrong end of lopsided Week 10 results could see their CFP hopes virtually vanish
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        How damaging is a blowout loss?It's one of the big lessons we'll learn when the College Football Playoff selection committee unveils its second rankings of the season on Tuesday night. Specifically, we're most interested in how the committee assesses Kentucky and Ole Miss. Both teams were ranked in the top 10 last week, and both teams suffered losses of 28 points or more on Saturday. If there's a silver lining to the two bad results, at least they came against teams ranked No. 2 (Georgia) and No. 13 (Tennessee) headed into the weekend. We know that both teams are going to drop. The question is how far? The two-loss Wildcats still have two top-25 wins (LSU, South Carolina) and rank in the top 10 in both strength of record and strength of schedule. Is that enough to keep Kentucky in the 12-team field? It feels like it should, especially with how the committee has approached the top SEC teams thus far, but a drop outside the top 12 would leave no margin for error with a schedule that still includes Florida, Missouri and Louisville.Ole Miss is in an even more precarious situation. Like the Wildcats, the Rebels have two impressive wins over top-25 opponents. A one-score loss to Texas isn't bad. But the 42-7 loss to Georgia, coupled with an earlier 52-28 loss to Florida, is quite damaging. Ole Miss' playoff hopes may now be hanging by a thread without much opportunity to solidify its resume. 
If the committee ranks Ole Miss in the top 15, there's still a faint hope. If Ole Miss lands behind teams like Iowa, USC and Oregon on Tuesday night, that's a wrap. Tuesday night's CFP Rankings release will not air in its normal 7 p.m. ET slot. The second release will air between Champions Classic games on ESPN. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 1 Georgia (8-1)Best win: AlabamaAfter Miami's loss over the weekend, the Bulldogs take over as the new top dog of the CFP. Georgia easily handled Ole Miss in one of the most impressive performances of the 2026 season. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 2 Utah (9-0)Best win: BYUIf Georgia is an obvious No. 1, Utah is just as obvious a No. 2 in these rankings. The Utes move up after a 28-20 win over in-state rival BYU. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 3 Alabama (7-2)Best win: KentuckyThe committee already loved Alabama even before its 31-13 road win over LSU. The Tide have three wins over top 25 teams. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 4 Indiana (8-1)Best win: NorthwesternThis is where it starts getting really interesting. The Hoosiers didn't play last weekend, but their resume suffered a hit as 8 of their 9 Big Ten opponents this season all lost. I could see Notre Dame, Miami and Texas all in this No. 4 spot over Indiana. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 5 Notre Dame (8-1)Best win: MiamiThe Fighting Irish badly needed a resume-building win and got one over Miami (albeit without star receiver Malachi Toney). It should be enough to jump Notre Dame several spots after opening the rankings at No. 11 last week. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 6 Texas (7-2)Best win: Ole MissThe Longhorns may have the best resume in the country with ranked wins over Tennessee, Ole Miss, Ohio State and now Missouri. A win over LSU this weekend, and Texas is all but guaranteed a playoff spot. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 7 Miami (8-1)Best win: Wake ForestThe Hurricanes should be fine -- and the committee may not drop them this far without Toney -- but the resume is missing a truly standout win other than a Week 2 win over Wake Forest. Miami does have good metrics, though, with the No. 4 strength-of-record in the country. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 8 UCLA (9-0)Best win: OregonThe undefeated Bruins have a great strength of record (No. 1) and an awful strength of schedule (No. 76). Illinois and USC are two more opportunities to add quality wins to a resume that needs them. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 9 Tennessee (7-2)Best win: AlabamaThe Volunteers crushed Kentucky, 34-6, to solidify themselves as a playoff team if the season ended today. The wins over Alabama and Kentucky are great, and the loss to South Carolina isn't as bad today, as the Gamecocks continue to win. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 10 Kentucky (7-2)Best win: LSUHow far the committee drops the Wildcats after a blowout loss could depend on whether it views the loss as an aberration or an indictment. It wouldn't be a shock to see Kentucky outside the top 12, but the metrics remain very favorable, and the committee clearly appreciates how strong the SEC is this season. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 11 BYU (7-2)Best win: Notre DameOne of the toughest decisions the committee will make is how to gauge BYU versus Texas Tech. The Cougars have the better win (Notre Dame) but also the much worse loss (UCF). BYU has a much better game control rating and strength of schedule, while Texas Tech has the edge in strength of record. We're giving BYU the slight edge here because the committee seems to value good wins more than bad losses. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 12 Texas Tech (8-1)Best win: HoustonThe Red Raiders are the first team out this week. Houston and Arizona continuing to win is a good sign for Texas Tech's chances, as would be a berth in the Big 12 Championship. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 13 Wake Forest (8-1)Best win: Louisville The Demon Deacons move up a few spots because of teams ranked above them losing over the weekend. Wake Forest has an important game coming up against SMU. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 14 Ole Miss (6-3)Best win: LSUThe 42-7 loss to Georgia was Ole Miss' second blowout of the season, which is bad for game-control discussions, and there aren't any big games left on the schedule. Ole Miss now only has a 10.3% chance to make the playoff, according to CBS Sports' forecasting model. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 15 Houston (7-2)Best win: Oklahoma State The Cougars should move up a few spots after a win over Cincinnati. Houston's playoff odds currently sit at 19.2%. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 16 Iowa (7-2)Best win: Wisconsin If the Hawkeyes keep winning, they're going to have a shot to sneak into the playoff. The odds aren't great (20%), but a 10-2 Iowa team would at least be in the conversation, especially if SEC and Big 12 teams keep beating up on each other. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 17 Oregon (6-3)Best win: Ohio StateThe Ducks have a head-to-head win over USC, which puts them one spot above the Trojans after beating Ohio State this weekend. The problem for Oregon is there isn't a quality win left on the schedule, so it'll need chaos to move up much more than this. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 18 USC (7-2)Best win: Ohio StateThe Trojans' marquee win of the season, Ohio State, took a hit, which isn't particularly helpful. But USC is still very much in the race, especially if it can get a win against either Indiana or UCLA this season. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 19 South Carolina (6-3)Best win: Tennessee Shane Beamer is dancing as the Gamecocks keep moving their way up the rankings. Florida losing this weekend hurts, but Tennessee's big win over Kentucky bolsters South Carolina's resume. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 20 Ohio State (6-3)Best win: IndianaWhile technically still in the mix, Ohio State's playoff hopes died in a stunning home loss to Oregon last weekend. The committee will not give a Julian Sayin-less OSU team the benefit of the doubt. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 21 Arizona (7-2)Best win: Cincinnati The Wildcats' resume is a bit thin but could get a big benefit with the Utah Utes up next. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 22 LSU (6-3)Best win: AuburnThe Tigers badly need a win over Texas this weekend to have any hope of staying in the playoff hunt. The loss to Alabama was damaging. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 23 Boise State (8-1)Best win: MemphisThe Broncos remain the pick to be the Group of Six's representative in the playoff. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 24 Missouri (6-3)Best win: Florida The Tigers drop six spots after a hard-fought loss to Texas. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    No. 25 Illinois (6-3)Best win: OregonIt's not the top 15, Bret Bielema, but at least you're on the list. Bracket based on first CFP Rankings predictionFirst roundDec. 18-19 at higher seedsNo. 12 Boise State at No. 5 Notre DameNo. 11 BYU at No. 6 TexasNo. 10 Kentucky at No. 7 MiamiNo. 9 Tennessee at No. 8 UCLAQuarterfinal matchupsDec. 30 in Glendale, Ariz., Jan. 1 in Atlanta, Arlington, Texas, and Pasadena, Calif. No. 1 Georgia  vs. No. 8 UCLA/No. 9 Tennessee winnerNo. 2 Utah vs. No. 7 Miami/No. 10 Kentucky winnerNo. 3 Alabama vs. No. 6 Texas/No. 11 BYU winnerNo. 4 Indiana vs. No. 5 Notre Dame/No. 12 Boise State winner

body:
Buffalo had a clear need in the secondary, and they addressed it with one of the NFL's best safeties
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026

    2:45 pm ET

                Getty Images
            
            

    
        The Buffalo Bills, who are the AFC's top seed through nine weeks with a 7-1 record, watched the Jacksonville Jaguars load up and decided they needed to make a splash before the 2026 NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday.They acquired Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker and a fifth-round pick while sending Tennessee a second-round pick, per an ESPN report. Hooker, who is 28 years old, leads the NFL in interceptions with five after picking off Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow three times in a 43-36 overtime defeat in Week 8. Hooker is just the third player in the past 40 years with 50-plus tackles (52) and 5-plus interceptions (5) in his first seven games of a season, along with Washington cornerback DeAngelo Hall (2010) and Indianapolis Colts linebacker Cato June (2005). He and Green Bay Packers All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney are also the only two players in the last three seasons with 200-plus tackles (204) and double-digit interceptions (10). Acquiring Hooker also came at a steep price because his three-year, $40.5 million contract is now a team-friendly asset that has him under team control through the 2028 season. This was a deal the Bills had to make, all things considered. Buffalo led the NFL in scoring defense with 19.3 points per game allowed from 2021 to 2025 under ex-head coach Sean McDermott, but under first-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard, they're allowing 23.4 points per game, ranking 16th in the league. They're also 14th in expected points added (EPA) per play and 17th in EPA per dropback, but those numbers were artificially deflated by Wentz and the wheezing Vikings offense. Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Bills were tied for 24th in scoring defense (25.9 points per game allowed), 24th in defensive EPA per play and 27th in EPA per dropback.  
On Monday night, Minnesota had open wide receivers throughout the game, but Wentz was unable to find them. That won't be the case against stiffer quarterback competition in the postseason. Teams are throwing at Buffalo's secondary at the second-highest rate in the NFL (62.6%) since they are allowing the fourth-most passing yards per game (238.8) in the league, per NFL Pro. That's why Buffalo parted with a second-round pick to acquire Hooker.

title: Jonathan Taylor mock trades: How Giants, Broncos, Vikings could target Colts star RB - CBS Sports
description: The Colts need to replenish their draft assets, and dealing their three-time Pro Bowl running back could produce
body:
The Colts need to replenish their draft assets, and dealing their three-time Pro Bowl running back could produce a significant return
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:24 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Indianapolis Colts are in free fall, having lost five straight games after a 2-2 start to the season. During the losing streak, Indianapolis has fired GM Chris Ballard (after the first of the five straight losses, to previously winless Titans) and traded two franchise cornerstones. Interim GM Ed Dodds shipped guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers.Trades often beget more trades -- or at least trade rumors, and that's been true for the Colts. Ahead of the trade deadline, plenty of Indianapolis players have been thought of as trade candidates, though one stands out above the rest: running back Jonathan Taylor.He had 20 touchdowns and nearly 2,000 yards from scrimmage last year, and he's on his way to another big season, but the Colts are stuck going nowhere once again. He's 27 and has played in just one playoff game -- as a rookie in 2020. He would command a huge return haul, and the Colts could very much use it, especially because they don't have their 2027 first-round pick (currently No. 4 overall) after last year's disastrous Sauce Gardner trade.Taylor would have plenty of suitors if made available, and the situation isn't too dissimilar from what the Panthers were going through with Christian McCaffrey in 2022. McCaffrey is a more versatile player than Taylor in the passing game and was younger than Taylor is now when that deal happened, but he had also been more injured. In the deal with the 49ers in 2022, Carolina received second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks.
With that in mind, here are four teams who could come calling about Taylor and what a mock trade might look like:
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York GiantsGiants receive: RB Jonathan TaylorColts receive: RB Cam Skattebo, 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pickLast month, John Harbaugh said he "would love" to have a "Derrick Henry circumstance or a "Saquon Barkley circumstance." Whether he meant to or not, it was surely a bummer for Giants fans to hear Harbaugh mention his running back from last year and a former Giants running back in the same sentence. Regardless, Taylor could be that type of workhorse. Harbaugh even confirmed the Giants put an offer in on Taylor but retracted it. The Colts getting two high draft picks over the next two years, plus Skattebo, who showed promise as a rookie but has had an up-and-down 2026, would be a decent return. The Giants are leading a bad NFC East, and even if it doesn't finish that way, having Taylor next to Jaxson Dart next year would be an enticing prospect.
One thing to note, though, is that Harbaugh comes from one of the most patient, draft-and-develop franchises in Baltimore. This would be a significant departure from that.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cincinnati BengalsBengals receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fifth-round pickColts receive: RB Chase Brown, 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pickThis would be similar to the package the Panthers got for McCaffrey, but instead of a third-round pick, the Colts would get Brown. At 26, he's younger and has less wear and tear than Taylor. He's also an accomplished player and productive pass catcher who has handled a bell-cow workload before. A change of scenery could do him good, as he has struggled to get going this season. For the Bengals, this would be a second major win-now move in just over six months; they sent the No. 10 pick to the Giants in April for Dexter Lawrence. The Bengals had tried to work in more under-center looks, but were among the worst teams using it. Now, they're once again a shotgun-heavy, pass-heavy team. In the playoffs or in iffy weather, though, they might need more balance. Cincinnati also has an extra third-round pick, which helps make giving up so many picks easier to swallow.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Denver BroncosBroncos receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 sixth-round pickColts receive: RB J.K. Dobbins, 2027 second-round pick, 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pickThe Broncos traded a first-round pick for an upgrade at wide receiver in Jaylen Waddle this offseason (though it hasn't really worked out yet). Would they make another big deal for an upgrade at running back in Taylor? The Broncos have struggled to muster much on the ground, exacerbating quarterback Bo Nix's struggles -- though Nix has been better of late. Dobbins is on a two-year deal, though there's an out after this year should the Colts choose to use it.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsVikings receive: RB Jonathan TaylorColts receive: RB Jordan Mason, 2027 second-round pick, 2027 third-round pick
The Vikings are in the quarterback market after an awful "Monday Night Football" loss to the Bills featured Carson Wentz throwing two picks with Kyler Murray (hamstring) sidelined. If they can't cash in there, though, perhaps they could try to upgrade the other part of their sagging offense. Mason would be a nice, young-ish piece for the Colts to get back to help the rest of the way. Plus, the Vikings have draft capital to spare, with an extra third, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.

title: Cooper Flagg beats LeBron James, Anthony Edwards to NBA history: How the Mavericks star leveled up - CBS Sports
description: Flagg is the first teenager in NBA history to record five 40-point games
body:
Flagg is the first teenager in NBA history to record five 40-point games
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 10, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With just over 30 seconds to play on Monday, Naji Marshall missed a free throw that would have put the Dallas Mavericks up by three, but secured the offensive rebound and kicked the ball out to Cooper Flagg. The 2026 Rookie of the Year took some time to assess the situation, then jab-stepped to his right and drove left. He took two dribbles and rose up over Andrew Nembhard, who could do little but hope he missed. Flagg did not miss. His mid-range jumper was pure and put the Mavericks up by four with 26 seconds left in an eventual 125-122 win over the Indiana Pacers. Flagg, who had been knocked out of the Mavericks' previous matchup with the Pacers this season by a flagrant foul from Aaron Nesmith, finished with a season-high 43 points, 10 rebounds, six assists and three steals on 16 of 25 from the field as the Mavericks won their third game in a row to improve to 7-4. In the process, Flagg became the first teenager in NBA history to record five 40-point games -- as many as LeBron James and Anthony Edwards combined. No one else besides those three has more than one 40-point game as a teenager. In addition, Flagg is now third all-time in total points scored before turning 20, behind only Kobe Bryant and James. Furthermore, Flagg joined Kevin Durant as the only teenagers to have a 40-point, 10-rebound, five-assist game. Most 40-point games as teenagersPlayer40-point gamesCooper Flagg5LeBron James3Anthony Edwards2For the season, Flagg is now averaging 25.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 6.9 assists and 2.2 steals, and that's despite leaving the first game against the Pacers early and an ice-cold 3 of 19 performance against the Sacramento Kings. He's 11th in the league in scoring, 16th in assists and fifth in steals. "He affects the game in so many ways, and he makes the right plays as far as passing. Thank goodness he's on our team," Mavericks coach Dusty May said after Monday's win. "It's unbelievable he's a 19-year-old doing this."
As May noted, Flagg is far more than just a scorer. But as he continues to establish himself as one of the best young scorers in NBA history, let's take a closer look at how he gets it done in that department. Most points in NBA history before turning 20PlayerPointsLeBron James2,362Kobe Bryant1,759Cooper Flagg1,732Carmelo Anthony1,725Crafty and efficient around the basketFlagg is 6-foot-9 and uses his size to get to the basket on a regular basis. He doesn't just bully opponents, though; he plays with a pace that's rare for his age, has great craft around the rim, and is more than willing to move off the ball. You need to look no further than Monday's outing against the Pacers to see how many different ways Flagg can score around the rim. He forced his way to the rim out of isolation, threw down a dunk in transition, attacked a closeout for another slam, cut back door and spun into another layup, drove to the basket out of the pick-and-roll, cut back door again for an easy finish and ran in transition for a double-clutch lefty finger roll. 
Flagg is taking six shots at the rim per game, per Synergy Sports, and shooting 61.7% on them. Among players that have taken at least 50 attempts at the rim this season, Flagg ranks 20th in efficiency. His ability to get into the paint also helps him earn trips to the free-throw line, where he's shooting 90.3%. Flagg's 7.2 free throw attempts per game rank 12th in the league, and are up from 4.9 per game as a rookie. In his rookie season, Flagg only had eight games with double-digit free throw attempts; he has three already this season. 
Getting to his spots at a 'higher level'Flagg put in extensive work on his mid-range game during the offseason, and it's paying major dividends to start the season. Not only has he increased his scoring output, but he's done so while taking less punishment. "I think just being able to get to my spots at a higher level, and being more comfortable with that, has allowed me to take a little bit of load off my body. Just kind of stopping short, raising up over people," Flagg said on Monday. "It's taxing to get downhill all the way to the rim and try and finish over seven-footers all night, every night. Just adding that in there definitely allows me to pace myself a little bit, steal some easy ones."Flagg's two clutch buckets late in the win over the Pacers were a perfect example of his improvement. SeasonPaint (Non-RA) FG%Mid-Range FG%OTD 2P FG%2025-2647.2%38%37.8%2026-2756.3%48.8%59.5%Flagg is 25 of 42 on off-the-dribble 2-point attempts this season. Among the seven players who have taken at least 40 such attempts, no one has been more efficient. While Flagg isn't going to shoot nearly 60% on pull-up 2s all season, it's clear that he's far more comfortable with his in-between game, which is a great sign for his development. "He's able to square in the air from 15, 17 feet. He can get to his spots, and if there's a smaller guy he can just jump and square in the air over them," May said. 3-point shot still needs workFlagg's growth inside the arc has allowed him to increase his scoring average by nearly five points per game despite the fact that his 3-point shot remains a work in progress. After shooting 29.5% as a rookie, he's shooting 29.2% this season on slightly more attempts. Flagg is shooting 30.8% on catch-and-shoot attempts and 31.6% on off-the-dribble attempts. Notably, he's also at just 31.6% on wide-open attempts. "Like the 3-point percentage obviously hasn't been great, but I still trust myself," Flagg said on Sunday. "I think my teammates trust me, my coaches. So I'm gonna keep shooting it, and I worked on it all summer. I worked on it all last year, so I'm not worried about anything."Flagg did shoot 38.5% from behind the arc in his lone collegiate season at Duke. That, combined with his elite free throw shooting, suggests that he won't be a sub-30% 3-point shooter forever. If Flagg does eventually become a more reliable shooter, that would be bad news for the rest of the league. In the last couple of games, he's made some 3s, and he's making all his free throws. "That's how you put up the 43 points, where you do a little bit of everything," May said after Monday's game. "He finished at the mid-range, he finished at the rim, he got to the line. He's getting to the line more than he has. He affects the game in so many ways, and he makes the right plays as far as passing. Thank goodness he's on our team. It's unbelievable he's a 19-year-old doing this."
